assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production FIVE-FACE ROOM-BOX TEXTURE ATLAS for ray-box interior mapping behind building windows in a realistic night-driving game. THIS IS A FLAT UNFOLDED TEXTURE SHEET, NOT A ROOM PHOTOGRAPH, NOT AN ISOMETRIC RENDER.
Format: square opaque RGB image, 1536 x 1536 requested, no transparency.
CRITICAL EXACT LAYOUT: split canvas into a rigid uniform 3 by 3 square grid, each cell EXACTLY one third of canvas width and height. Five occupied cells form a plus sign:
row 1: PURE BLACK unused cell | CEILING surface | PURE BLACK unused cell
row 2: LEFT WALL surface | BACK WALL surface | RIGHT WALL surface
row 3: PURE BLACK unused cell | FLOOR surface | PURE BLACK unused cell
All four black corner cells MUST be full exact squares aligned at 1/3 and 2/3 image coordinates. No padding, borders, gaps or drawn grid lines inside this layout. Each occupied square is ONE face texture extending edge-to-edge. Do not change cell sizes or create a collage.
Face directions: back wall is viewed straight on with image up equal room up. Side walls are flat orthographic wall elevations, not perspective views. LEFT wall horizontal axis runs FRONT at left edge to BACK at right edge. RIGHT wall horizontal axis runs BACK at left edge to FRONT at right edge. CEILING is viewed straight up in a flat texture projection; FRONT is its top edge and BACK is its bottom edge. FLOOR is viewed straight down, BACK is its top edge and FRONT is its bottom edge. Floor and ceiling image right match back wall image right.
Look: realistic modest furnished urban interior, material grain and restrained indoor nighttime lighting, readable broad details seen through a distant building window. Five related surfaces of ONE consistent rectangular room, no wraparound photographic perspective. Match wall/floor colors at corresponding corners. Furniture may appear as shallow front-on detail on the back wall but must not be shown twice on multiple faces. Furniture and shadows stay within their own cell. Keep face corners simple so small seams are unobtrusive.
Constraints: no exterior window frame, no glass, no mullions, no curtains or blinds, no people, no exterior scenery, no visible front wall, no camera, no bright blown-out fixtures, no text, no labels, no logos, no watermark. No cubemap sixth face. Four unused corner cells pure black. No perspective room box or folded 3D geometry. This is directly usable surface texture art on a precise plus-shaped atlas.
Room: modest warm apartment living room with muted cream plaster walls and medium brown wood flooring. Back wall: a low muted olive sofa seen straight-on along the lower portion, a small framed abstract print above it and a short side cabinet at the right. A small warm shaded lamp on the cabinet gives a restrained amber light pool. Side walls: same cream plaster with sparse subtle detail, no additional sofa. Ceiling: flat cream with one small central warm light fitting. Floor: top-down medium brown wooden boards oriented front-to-back, a small muted plain rug near the back half, no perspective. Restrained amber-white lighting, not orange, not saturated.
assets.refinement_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a five-face room texture atlas.
Correct its face projections for actual ray-box texture mapping while preserving this room's identity, furnishings, muted lighting, palette and exact 3x3 plus-sign tile layout.
IMPORTANT: the THREE cells in the middle row are wall surface maps. Every pixel in each of those square cells MUST belong to its one flat wall elevation. Remove ALL visible floor strips, ALL ceiling strips, ALL wedge-shaped adjacent-wall corners and ALL converging perspective lines from those cells. Replace those areas with matching flat wall material. Keep a single thin perfectly horizontal baseboard at the exact bottom of each wall cell, and a thin horizontal trim at its top. Middle-left is a flat plain wall, middle-center a flat straight-on back wall with its furnishings seen as front elevations, middle-right a flat plain wall with its original wall-mounted detailing seen directly head-on. Furniture can occupy the lower back-wall cell but NO perspective view of the floor behind it.
Top-center ceiling cell must be flat overhead surface viewed square-on, no trapezoid, no perspective molding, no diagonal lines, no walls visible. Preserve its small light fixture in direct overhead view.
Bottom-center floor cell remains a pure top-down floor material, no walls, no furniture duplicated on it.
Preserve exactly FOUR pure black corner squares with boundaries at exactly 1/3 and 2/3 of image width and height. Keep five equal square face cells. No text, no labels, no borders. This must be an opaque flat unfolded texture atlas, not a room photograph or perspective render.
